The schema version an atlas was built against

Source: R/atlas_schema.R
atlas_schema_version.Rd

A serialized S7 object carries a frozen copy of its class: the properties, the constructor and the validator as they stood when the object was built. That is what lets an atlas saved by one release load under another, and it is also the trap. Add a property to ggseg_atlas and an atlas built before it does not merely lack the property – reading it is a hard error, while S7::validate() still passes, because the validator it runs is the one frozen inside it. The atlas looks fine, dispatches fine, and fails only when something touches the new property.

Usage

atlas_schema_version()

atlas_schema(atlas)

atlas_schema_is_current(atlas)

Arguments

atlas

a ggseg_atlas object

Value

atlas_schema_version() returns a single integer. atlas_schema() returns the version an atlas was built against, or 0L for an atlas built before the stamp existed – including every legacy list atlas. atlas_schema_is_current() returns a logical scalar.

Details

Nothing in S7 detects that, so the atlas carries its own stamp. Every atlas records the schema version it was built against; atlas_schema_version() is what the installed ggseg.formats builds today. When the two differ, as_ggseg_atlas() rebuilds the atlas through the current constructor, which fills in whatever is new and revalidates against current rules.

This matters because atlases are published, not just made: roughly 150 of them live in R/sysdata.rda files across the atlas packages, each built by whichever ggseg.formats was current that day, and r-universe rebuilds them on its own schedule.

When to bump

Bump atlas_schema_version() whenever an atlas built by the previous version would be wrong, or incomplete, under the current one: a property added or removed, an invariant tightened, a slot's meaning changed. Do not bump for a new accessor, a new verb, or a bug fix that leaves stored data alone – a bump costs every published atlas a rebuild or an upgrade.

See also

as_ggseg_atlas(), which upgrades a stale atlas.

Other atlas accessors: atlas_centerlines(), atlas_context(), atlas_core(), atlas_data(), atlas_display(), atlas_geom(), atlas_geometry_type(), atlas_hemi(), atlas_labels(), atlas_meshes(), atlas_name(), atlas_palette(), atlas_plot_palette(), atlas_polygons(), atlas_provenance(), atlas_region_semantics(), atlas_regions(), atlas_sf(), atlas_type(), atlas_undrawn(), atlas_vertices(), atlas_views(), atlas_views_empty(), has_atlas_geometry, legacy_region_map()

Examples

atlas_schema_version()
#> [1] 1
atlas_schema(dk())
#> [1] 1
atlas_schema_is_current(dk())
#> [1] TRUE
